---
title: "Run it yourself"
---

Every page on this site is built from notebooks you can run on your own CUDA GPU.

## Requirements

- Linux with an NVIDIA GPU and a recent driver (tested: driver 580, CUDA 13.0)
- [juliaup](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup) (the project pins Julia 1.12)
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for the Python/JAX environment
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) ≥ 1.10
- `make`

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/michel2323/WEANJ
cd WEANJ
make setup
```

`make setup` installs the Julia 1.12 channel, instantiates and precompiles the Julia
environment in `julia/` (Enzyme, Reactant, CUDA), creates the Python environment in
`python/` (JAX with CUDA 13), and writes `_environment.local` so Quarto uses that
Python. The first run downloads several GB and takes 10–15 minutes.

## Check the toolchain

```bash
quarto render smoke/
```

This runs a tiny gradient on the GPU with each of the three tools. Open
`_site/smoke/index.html`; all three tabs should show output.

## Run the examples

```bash
quarto preview                      # browse the site, edit and re-run notebooks live
quarto render examples/01-particles/enzyme.qmd   # re-run one notebook
make run-gpu                        # re-run everything; refreshes _freeze/ and benchmarks/
```

Rendering a single notebook always executes it. Rendering the whole site uses the frozen
outputs in `_freeze/`, so it does not need a GPU.

## Troubleshooting

**JAX prints `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`**
: Another process is using the GPU. The notebooks disable JAX's up-front memory
  reservation, but benchmark numbers are only meaningful on an idle GPU:
  `make gpu-check` lists what is running.

**Julia version mismatch**
: The notebooks start Julia with `julia +1.12`. Run `juliaup add 1.12`.
